takeaway: Another hot, mostly sunny day. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds on the North Pacific this morning, light winds early, and a few clouds building this afternoon with only an isolated shower in the hills. Nicoya should hit about 35°C. For surf, it's offshore again today and every day through at least Tuesday, with a south-southwest swell at 5–7 feet and 15 seconds today, easing to 3–5 feet by Sunday, then a new longer-period pulse showing up Tuesday night. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The models are still pointing to a wetter spell around Nov 2–5, now a little earlier and a little stronger, while IMN still calls for the dry season to arrive in early November. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Fri–Sun, Oct 23–25)
periods.pattern: IMN's Friday forecast for the North Pacific is few clouds in the early morning and morning, partly cloudy in the afternoon with an isolated shower in the mountains, and partly cloudy tonight. Nicoya's high is about 35°C (Liberia and Puntarenas near 34.5°C) with a low around 23°C. IMN says the day starts with light winds and quickly rising temperatures, with clouds building after midday but little rain. The model averages show light rain near Nosara: roughly 5–10 mm (0.2–0.4 inch) today, then a few millimeters Saturday and Sunday. The marine forecast mentions scattered offshore showers and a few storms Saturday and Saturday night.
periods.implications: Good beach and outdoor days. It'll be hot by late morning, so do active things early. A brief shower is possible, most likely in the hills or overnight, and shouldn't spoil plans.
periods.confidence: High on hot, mostly sunny days. Moderate on whether a stray shower reaches the coast on Saturday.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Mon–Thu, Oct 26–29)
periods.pattern: Every model keeps a steady northeast-to-east breeze over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica. Rain near Nosara drops to just a few millimeters a day or less, with the heavier rain on the Caribbean side and well offshore to the south. IMN's weekly outlook describes the switch from rainy to dry season, with trade-wind gusts of 40–60 km/h in the mornings that ease in the afternoons, and a chance of isolated showers on the Pacific coast at night.
periods.implications: Likely the driest stretch so far this season. Expect sunny days, breezy mornings, and lower humidity. Good for outdoor plans.
periods.confidence: High on mostly dry and breezy.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Fri Oct 30 – Fri Nov 6)
periods.pattern: The trades keep blowing over Nicaragua in every model into early November, but the band of tropical showers that sits south of Costa Rica drifts back north toward the Nicoya coast. The American average now starts this a bit earlier, with about 10 mm (0.4 inch) near Nosara on Oct 31 and close to an inch a day on Nov 2 and again Nov 4. The European average has about 10 mm on Nov 2 and close to an inch on Nov 4, easing by Nov 6. The AI-based European average is lighter, around 10 mm a day. The regular European model run stays mostly dry through Nov 2. IMN's long-range outlook (Oct 26–Nov 22) still calls for drier-than-normal weather nationwide, extra-dry on the North Pacific, and the dry season taking hold on the North and Central Pacific in the first week of November.
periods.implications: The end of October looks good. Keep plans for roughly Nov 2–5 flexible, since that's when the models show the best chance of a few wet days, and IMN disagrees.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on a dry end to October. Low on early November.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, offshore at Nosara, every day from today through at least Tuesday. It's a steady offshore pattern, a bit lighter than it looked yesterday for Monday.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 12:59 a.m. PDT Friday, 1:59 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds at 15–20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo today and northeast 10–15 knots elsewhere, which is offshore here. Tonight it's northeast around 10. Saturday and Saturday night it's northeast to east 15–20 in the gulf and about 10 elsewhere, with scattered offshore showers and a few storms. Sunday is northeast to east 10–15, and Monday is northeast 10–15 (yesterday's forecast had Monday at 20–25 in the gulf). Tuesday is northeast to east around 10. One caution: the waters just south of the peninsula have southwest winds around 10 knots today through Monday, and Nosara sits near that edge, so afternoon sea breeze can add texture, especially on lighter days. IMN also notes light winds this morning on land. Swell: south to southwest 5–7 feet at 15 seconds today, 4–6 feet at 15 seconds tonight, 4–6 feet at 14 seconds Saturday, 3–5 feet at 13 seconds Sunday, 3–5 feet at 11 seconds Monday, then the period climbs to 14 seconds Tuesday and 16 seconds Tuesday night, a sign of a new long-period south swell arriving. Nicaragua: every model keeps solid easterly trades over Nicaragua for the next two weeks, so Nicaragua should be offshore all day most days. That's a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean Nosara is offshore all day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today and Saturday mornings: the best of the run, offshore with the 15-second swell at 4–7 feet. Go early. Sunday and Monday mornings: still offshore and clean, but smaller and shorter-period at 3–5 feet. Tuesday night into Wednesday: watch for the new long-period pulse, with offshore wind still in place. Long-period sets come bigger and less often than the average height suggests.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore through Tuesday from the marine forecast. High on the swell trend through Monday, moderate on the size of the Tuesday-night pulse. Moderate on how late into each afternoon the offshore holds.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, low. Nothing established and nothing building in the next 10 days. The early-November wet signal got slightly stronger but still doesn't look like a prolonged-rain setup.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Around Nov 2–5, at the far end of the forecast.
gyreWatch.supporting: All three model averages bring the shower band south of Costa Rica north toward Nicoya in early November. The American average shows close to an inch a day near Nosara on Nov 2 and Nov 4, and the European average close to an inch on Nov 4. The American average also shows a weak low south of Guatemala late in the period.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model shows a broad, slow-spinning low parked near Costa Rica, and all of them keep northeast-to-east trades over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November. A multi-day soak usually needs days of steady wind off the Pacific, which is the opposite. The regular European run stays mostly dry through Nov 2. IMN's long-range outlook calls for drier-than-normal weather through Nov 22 and sees no extreme events Oct 26–Nov 1. Hurricane Vance is several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco and moving away, and the U.S. hurricane center expects no new storms in the Caribbean or near Central America in the next week.

whatChanged: Monday's offshore winds in the marine forecast came down from 20–25 knots in the gulf to 10–15, and the offshore pattern now runs through Tuesday. Today's swell is 5–7 feet at 15 seconds (yesterday was 17 seconds), and the marine forecast now hints at a new long-period south swell arriving Tuesday night. Vance strengthened into a hurricane but is moving away from Central America. IMN's new weekly outlook says we're in the transition to the dry season, with gusty morning trades. The early-November wet signal in the models held and moved slightly earlier, with the American average now showing heavier rain near Nosara by Nov 2 instead of Nov 3–4.
practical: Today and Saturday: surf early in offshore wind and a solid 15-second swell, then expect a hot afternoon around 35°C. Sunday through Thursday: dry, breezy, sunny days, good for outdoor plans, with smaller but clean surf. Keep an eye out for a new swell Tuesday night into Wednesday. Keep Nov 2–5 plans flexible. Long-period swell means stronger currents, so watch for rips. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
